options.title: Elastic Integration Settings
options.description: Configure the polling and publishing settings for the Elastic integration.

data.publish_frequency: Send events to Elasticsearch at this interval
data.polling_frequency: Gather all entity states at this interval
data.change_detection_type: Choose what types of entity changes to listen for and publish
data.tags: Tags to apply to all published events
data.include_targets: Toggle to only publish the set of targets below
data.exclude_targets: Toggle to exclude publishing the set of targets below

data_description.publish_frequency: Set to zero to disable publishing.
data_description.polling_frequency: Set to zero to only publish entity changes.
data_description.publish_query_sensors: Off by default to avoid feeding derived readings back into their source queries. When enabled, normal target filters still apply.

unsupported_version.message: This version of Elasticsearch is not supported. The minimum supported version is {minimum_version}. Upgrade the cluster, then reload the entry.

unsupported_server.message: This endpoint does not provide the required Elasticsearch server information. Connect to a supported Elasticsearch cluster, then reload the entry.

invalid_ca_certificate.message: The certificate authority file {ca_path} could not be loaded. Check that the file is a readable, PEM-encoded certificate, or reconfigure the entry.

authentication_failed.message: Elasticsearch rejected the credentials, or they lack the required privileges.

integration_error.message: Unable to set up the integration: {error}

unexpected_error.message: An unexpected error occurred. Check the Home Assistant logs for details.

query_not_supported.message: Querying requires Elasticsearch {minimum_version}, but this cluster runs {version}. Publishing still works. Upgrade the cluster to run queries.

query_ambiguous_columns.message: The query returns more than one column named {columns}. Give each column a unique name, for example with RENAME or EVAL.

query_too_many_rows.message: The query returned {rows} rows, more than the limit of {limit}. Add a LIMIT, or summarize the rows with STATS.

query_truncated.message: The query has no LIMIT, so Elasticsearch stopped at its default of {limit} rows and the result may be incomplete. Add a LIMIT of at most {max_rows}, or summarize the rows with STATS.

query_result_too_large.message: The query's result is {size}, more than the limit of {limit}. Return fewer rows or columns, for example with LIMIT or KEEP.

query_partial_result.message: Elasticsearch could only return partial results for the query, so they were discarded. Check the cluster's health, then try again.

query_cancelled.message: The query was cancelled because its Elasticsearch entry was unloaded or reloaded. Try again once the entry has loaded.

query_invalid_response.message: Elasticsearch returned a query response that couldn't be read.

query_insufficient_privileges.message: The entry's credentials aren't allowed to run this query. Grant them the read privilege on the indices the query reads.

query_timeout.message: Elasticsearch didn't answer the query within {timeout} seconds.

sensor_empty_query.message: Enter a name and a non-empty ES|QL query.

sensor_invalid_params.message: Parameters must be a JSON array of strings, finite numbers, booleans, or nulls.

sensor_multiple_rows.message: The query returned multiple rows. Use an aggregation, or explicitly SORT and LIMIT 1 to select the intended observation.

sensor_missing_column.message: The selected value column is missing. Reconfigure the sensor and select a column by name.

sensor_invalid_value.message: The selected column must contain one supported scalar: a finite number or text of at most 255 characters. Booleans, objects, arrays, and values incompatible with the sensor metadata are not supported. Use ES|QL to convert or extract the value.

sensor_invalid_metadata.message: Choose a compatible device class, unit, and state class. Numeric metadata requires a numeric column; date, timestamp, and uptime sensors cannot have a unit or state class.

sensor_invalid_freshness.message: Set both an observation timestamp column and a maximum source-data age, or leave both empty.

sensor_invalid_timestamp.message: The observation must be a valid date/date_nanos timestamp with a timezone, no later than the current time.

sensor_stale.message: The source observation is older than the configured maximum age. Check the source data or adjust the freshness requirement.

sensor_query_warnings.message: Elasticsearch returned execution warnings, which may mean values were ignored or calculations failed. Run the query action to inspect its warnings and correct the query.

sensor_insufficient_privileges.message: The credentials cannot read the requested data. Grant read access to the indices named in FROM.

sensor_authentication_failed.message: Elasticsearch rejected the credentials. Reauthenticate the connection.

sensor_query_not_supported.message: Querying requires Elasticsearch 8.19+ on 8.x or 9.1+ on 9.x. Supported publishing can continue on older versions.

sensor_query_rejected.message: Elasticsearch rejected the query. Check its syntax, parameters, source fields, and server-supported functions using the query action.

sensor_query_timeout.message: The query exceeded the connection request timeout. Simplify the query or check cluster health.

sensor_cannot_connect.message: The query could not reach Elasticsearch. Check the connection and cluster health. Polling will retry automatically.

sensor_query_failed.message: The query failed or returned an invalid, partial, or oversized response. Check cluster health and try the query action for details.

duplicate_cluster.title: Two entries publish to the same Elasticsearch cluster
duplicate_cluster.description:
The entries **{entry_title}** and **{other_title}** both publish to the same Elasticsearch cluster, so the same Home Assistant data is sent to it twice.

Remove one of the entries from the Elasticsearch integration page. This issue clears once only one of them is left.

unsupported_version.title: Elasticsearch {version} is not supported
unsupported_version.description:
**{entry_title}** connects to Elasticsearch {version}, but this integration requires version {minimum_version} or later. Nothing is published until the cluster is upgraded.

Upgrade the cluster, then reload the entry from the Elasticsearch integration page. This issue clears once the entry loads.

query.title: Query sensor
query.description: Enter a static ES|QL query that returns at most one row. The next step runs it and previews the result.

data_description.name: A name you choose; changing it preserves entity identity and history.
data_description.query: Select sources in FROM. Use STATS for a summary, or SORT ... DESC | LIMIT 1 for the latest observation.
data_description.params: An ordered JSON array bound to ? placeholders, for example ["sensor.outdoor_temperature"]. No templates or interpolation.

empty.title: No observations yet
empty.description: The query executed successfully but returned no rows. Continue to choose from its column metadata. The sensor will be unknown until an observation arrives.

mapping.title: Preview and sensor settings
mapping.description:
| Column | ES\|QL type | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
{preview}

Preview shows up to 30 columns and 256 characters per cell. All columns and full values are validated. An empty table means there are no current observations.

data_description.value_column: Select the scalar by column name. Additional columns are allowed and are not copied to attributes.
data_description.scan_interval: 10–86400 seconds; defaults to 60. Only one poll per sensor runs at a time.
data_description.unit_of_measurement: Optional. Use a unit accepted by the device class; no physical units are inferred.
data_description.device_class: Optional. Describes the physical measurement, or a date/timestamp value (including an uptime start timestamp).
data_description.state_class: Optional. Choose measurement, total, or total_increasing only when the query has the corresponding statistics semantics.
data_description.timestamp_column: Optional date/date_nanos column describing when the source observation occurred. Requires a maximum age.
data_description.max_age: 1–31536000 seconds. A reading becomes unavailable at this age even between polls. Requires an observation timestamp column.
